title: Vanishing of an ideal-power product is detected by affine-cover annihilators
statement: Let X be a scheme, F a quasi-coherent O_X-module, K a quasi-coherent ideal sheaf encoded by IdealSheafData, S a set of affine opens covering every point of X, and t a natural number. With ideal powers and their products as in [lem-weil-pbc-ideal-module-product-stalk], K^t F is zero if and only if, for every U in S, K(U)^t is contained in the annihilator of the O_X(U)-module F(U). The convention is K^0=O_X. No finiteness or Noetherian hypothesis is assumed.

source.place: Lemma 01Y9, proof: reduction to an affine covering; affine comparison from Schemes 01I8 and 01IC. The detailed zero-detection argument is the parent node steps 3 and 4.

proof.text: On an affine open U, identify the quasi-coherent ideal and F with tilde of their section modules I and M. Restriction preserves quasi-coherence and the tilde/Gamma counit is an isomorphism. The tensor-section comparison identifies multiplication with a tensor map sending a tensor m to am; the affine image formula identifies its image with IM.

Induct on t for the recursive shared idealSheafPower: the positive powers are quasi-coherent and have section image I^t by the ideal-times lemma; multiplication by their inclusion has section image I^t M by the tensor and image formulas of step 1. At t=0 the inclusion is the identity of the structure sheaf and multiplication is the left unitor, so its image is F. Thus its image sections are M=I^0 M. This obtains the product-sections identification at every natural exponent, including zero.
I^t M is the submodule generated by am for a in I^t and m in M. This submodule is zero if and only if each such am is zero, which is exactly I^t contained in Ann(M).

The product sheaf is quasi-coherent by steps 1 and 2. Its restriction to each covering affine is zero exactly when its section module is zero: the tilde/Gamma counit is an isomorphism and tilde, a left adjoint, preserves the zero module. If all restrictions are zero, restrict any section on W to W intersect U for each member U of the cover. These intersections cover W, every restriction is zero, and separatedness gives the original section zero. This proves the sheaf is zero. Conversely restricting a zero sheaf yields zero sections. The argument also applies to the empty cover on the empty scheme.

lean.statement:
theorem idealPowerProduct_isZero_iff_affine_cover (X : Scheme.{u})
    (F : X.Modules) [F.IsQuasicoherent] (K : X.IdealSheafData)
    (S : Set X.affineOpens) (hS : ∀ x : X, ∃ U ∈ S, x ∈ U.1) (t : ℕ) :
    IsZero (idealModuleProduct (idealSheafPower K.toModulesι t).2 F) ↔
      ∀ U ∈ S, K.ideal U ^ t ≤ Module.annihilator Γ(X, U.1) Γ(F, U.1)
